concept_card.subtopic: Velocity and acceleration of a particle in SHM
concept_card.learning_objective: Students will be able to state and explain where the speed and the acceleration of an ideal simple harmonic oscillator are maximum and zero, give the direction of the acceleration, and calculate v and a at any displacement.
concept_card.statement: In ideal SHM the speed is greatest at the mean position and zero at the extremes, while the acceleration is zero at the mean, greatest at the extremes, and always directed toward the mean.
concept_card.simple: Think of a block on a spring. In the middle the spring is relaxed, so nothing pushes the block and it is moving fastest. At the ends it stops for an instant, but the spring is stretched most, so the pull back is strongest there.
concept_card.formal: For x = A cos(ωt + φ), the velocity is v = −Aω sin(ωt + φ) = ±ω√(A² − x²) and the acceleration is a = −ω²x. Speed is therefore maximum (Aω) at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A. Acceleration is proportional to displacement and opposite to it: zero at the mean and of maximum magnitude ω²A at the extremes. Velocity and acceleration are out of phase by π/2, so one is largest when the other is zero.

equations.meaning: velocity at time t for x = A cos(ωt + φ)
speed at displacement x; maximum Aω at x = 0, zero at x = ±A
acceleration is proportional to displacement and points toward the mean; zero at x = 0, magnitude ω²A at x = ±A
kinetic energy is greatest at the mean position and zero at the extremes

concept_card.analogy: A child on a jhoola: she whooshes fastest through the bottom, where nothing tugs her forward or back, and pauses at the highest points, where the pull back down toward the bottom is strongest.
steps: Locate the oscillator: find its displacement x from the mean position.
Acceleration follows displacement: a = −ω²x, so it is zero at x = 0, largest at x = ±A, and always points toward the mean.
Speed follows the opposite pattern: v = ω√(A² − x²), so it is largest at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A.
Zero velocity does not mean zero acceleration: at the extremes the body is only turning around.
Check with energy: at the mean all energy is kinetic; at the extremes all is potential.
concept_card.worked_example: A block oscillates with A = 0.1 m and ω = 10 rad/s. At the mean: v = Aω = 1 m/s, a = 0. At an extreme: v = 0, |a| = ω²A = 100 × 0.1 = 10 m/s², toward the mean. At x = 0.06 m: v = 10√(0.01 − 0.0036) = 10 × 0.08 = 0.8 m/s and a = −100 × 0.06 = −6 m/s².
alternatives: Use force: the spring force F = −kx is zero at the mean and largest at the extremes, so by F = ma the acceleration follows the same pattern. The block speeds up while moving toward the mean and slows down after passing it, so its speed peaks exactly at the mean.

Use the circle: SHM is the shadow of uniform circular motion. At the centre of the shadow's path the point on the circle moves parallel to the line, so the shadow moves fastest; at the ends it moves perpendicular, so the shadow stops while the centripetal pull is fully along the line.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: It goes fastest at the ends because that's the farthest it gets.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Farthest sounds like the most of everything, so the biggest displacement feels like the biggest speed.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Displacement and speed are different. At an extreme the block stops for an instant to turn back; all its energy is in the spring.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Speed is maximum (Aω) at the mean position and zero at the extremes.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Pause at x = +A and read v = 0; then watch v peak as x passes 0.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: The speed stays the same all through the oscillation.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: The motion looks smooth and repeats evenly, so it seems steady.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Repeating evenly means a fixed period, not a fixed speed. The restoring force speeds the block up toward the mean and slows it beyond.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Speed varies as v = ω√(A² − x²): largest at the mean, zero at the extremes.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Watch the v readout and v–t graph rise and fall every half cycle.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: At the end it has stopped, so its acceleration is zero there.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Stopped feels like nothing is happening, and we link acceleration with moving.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. At the extreme the velocity is reversing, and the spring force is largest.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: At the extremes v = 0 but the acceleration is maximum (ω²A), pointing toward the mean.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Step through x = +A: v reads 0 while the acceleration arrow is longest, pointing to the centre.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: The acceleration is biggest in the middle, where it moves fastest.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Big speed and big acceleration both feel like 'a lot of motion', so they seem to go together.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Acceleration comes from force. At the mean the spring is unstretched, so the force, and the acceleration, is zero even at top speed.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Acceleration a = −ω²x is zero at the mean and largest at the extremes.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Pause at x = 0: speed is at its peak, the acceleration readout is 0.

contrast_probes.probe: Is the block's speed at the extreme position bigger than, equal to, or smaller than its speed at the mean position?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Bigger — it's fastest at the extreme.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Equal — the speed is the same everywhere.

contrast_probes.probe: What is the block's velocity at the instant it reaches the extreme position?
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It's zero there, so its acceleration is zero too.

contrast_probes.probe: At the mean position, is the block moving at its slowest or fastest?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Slowest — it's fastest at the ends.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Fastest, and that's why its acceleration is biggest there.

contrast_probes.probe: Does the block ever stop, even for an instant, during one oscillation?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, it keeps going at the same speed all the time.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, at the ends it stops, so it has no acceleration there.

contrast_probes.probe: Does the block's speed change as it moves from an extreme to the mean position?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, it stays the same throughout.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, it speeds up, and the acceleration is biggest when it reaches the mean.

contrast_probes.probe: Compare the block's acceleration at the extreme position with its acceleration at the mean position.
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It's zero at the extreme because the block stops there.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It's biggest at the mean because the block is fastest there.

contrast_probes.probe: Where is the block's kinetic energy largest, and where does it move fastest?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It moves fastest at the extreme, the farthest point.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Both at the mean position, where all the energy is kinetic.

contrast_probes.probe: Does the spring's force change the block's speed during an oscillation?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, the speed stays constant; only the direction flips.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, it speeds the block up toward the mean and slows it down beyond.

contrast_probes.probe: At the instant the block stops at an extreme, is any force acting on it?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: No, it's at rest, so there's no force and no acceleration.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Yes, the spring force is largest, so the acceleration is largest, toward the mean.

contrast_probes.probe: How much is the spring stretched when the block is at the mean position?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: It doesn't matter; the block is fastest there, so acceleration is biggest.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Not at all, so there's no force and the acceleration is zero.

doubts.q: How can the acceleration be maximum when the velocity is zero?
doubts.a: Acceleration measures how fast velocity changes, not how big it is. At an extreme the velocity is switching from one direction to the other, and the spring force is largest there, so the acceleration is largest even though v = 0 for an instant.

doubts.q: If the acceleration is zero at the mean position, why doesn't the block stop there?
doubts.a: Zero acceleration means the velocity is not changing at that instant, not that the velocity is zero. The block arrives at the mean with its maximum speed and carries on past it, then the restoring force starts slowing it down.

doubts.q: Is the acceleration always opposite to the velocity in SHM?
doubts.a: No. The acceleration always points toward the mean, but the velocity points toward the mean only on the way in. While moving toward the mean they are in the same direction and the body speeds up; while moving away they are opposite and it slows down.

doubts.q: Why is there a minus sign in a = −ω²x?
doubts.a: The minus sign shows the acceleration is always opposite to the displacement, that is, always directed toward the mean position. When x is positive a is negative, and when x is negative a is positive.

verify_flags: Jhoola analogy and P2 pendulum use the small-angle approximation; at the lowest point a real pendulum still has a centripetal acceleration v²/L, ignored in the SHM model.
Circle-projection alternative: confirm phrasing suits Class 11 reference-circle treatment.
